name: Tamsulosin US pivotal studies
question: Does once-daily tamsulosin improve symptoms and peak urinary flow compared with placebo in men with symptomatic BPH?

design.population: 756 men aged at least 45 years with symptomatic BPH, AUA symptom score at least 13, Qmax 4–15 mL/s, and postvoid residual below 300 mL were randomized; recent urinary retention and significant cardiovascular disease were excluded.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria and Patient Demographics, pp 893–894

verdictNote: All four primary measures improved with both doses; abnormal ejaculation increased with dose.
takeaway: In 756 randomized men with symptomatic BPH, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily or 0.4 mg for 1 week then 0.8 mg daily improved all four prespecified symptom and flow measures versus placebo at 13 weeks; abnormal ejaculation increased with dose.
